short_en: Because faith is about what is true, and truth can be shared. The people we love have real questions; giving reasons shows them faith is not a blind leap. St Peter asks every Christian to be ready to explain the hope inside them, with gentleness and respect (1 Pt 3:15).
short_ar: لأنّ الإيمان يتعلّق بالحقيقة، والحقيقة تُشارَك. مَن نحبّهم يحملون أسئلة حقيقية، وحين نقدّم لهم أسبابنا نُريهم أنّ الإيمان ليس قفزة في العتمة. القدّيس بطرس يطلب من كل مسيحي أن يكون مستعدّاً ليشرح الرجاء الذي فيه، بوداعة واحترام.
share_en: I didn't stop thinking to believe. I believe, and I can tell you why.
share_ar: لم أتوقّف عن التفكير لكي أؤمن. أنا أؤمن، وأستطيع أن أقول لك لماذا.
anim: A young man walks through doors marked with Greek philosophy schools that close one by one; by the sea an old man points to a light; Justin's scroll flies to the emperor's palace, then turns into a phone sending a WhatsApp message.

en.story:
Around the year 100, a boy is born near ancient Shechem, in Samaria (today's Nablus). Justin grows up hungry for truth and tries one school of Greek philosophy after another. Then an old man he meets on a seashore turns his search toward Christ. Justin becomes a Christian, opens a free school in Rome, and writes open letters, his Apologies, to the emperor himself. Around 165 he is beheaded for his faith. (Benedict XVI, General Audience, 21 Mar 2007) His demand to Rome was simple: investigate the charges against Christians before you condemn them. (First Apology, ch. 3)

Honest note: Justin's own story of his conversion may be partly stylized; his writings and his martyrdom are well attested.
en.deeper: The course opens with this verse: Christians must be ready to give a reason for the hope within us (SoA God, Introduction, p. 7). Many people think God can only be "taken on faith" because no one ever showed them the objective reasons (SoA God, Introduction, p. 8). Natural theology helps most those raised in cultures hostile to religion (SoA God L1, p. 10). The Church trusts reason so much that she believes we can speak about God "to all men and with all men": other religions, scientists, unbelievers and atheists (CCC 39). Writing to the Christians of the Middle East from Lebanon, Benedict XVI added how: defend the faith with sensitivity and respect for persons, but also with frankness and courage (Ecclesia in Medio Oriente 92). Apologetics is not about winning. It is love that gives answers.
en.proof:
• History: Justin's First Apology (c. 155), written to a pagan emperor, holds one of the oldest descriptions of the Sunday Eucharist: readings, homily, prayers, bread and wine. The Catechism quotes it as the basic shape of the Mass (CCC 1345; First Apology, ch. 67). Reasons given openly became a witness for all history.
  • Today: in a 2016 Pew Research report, 49% of Americans who left the religion they were raised in said a lack of belief led them away; many named science or "lack of evidence." (Pew Research Center) Unanswered questions push people out. Note: US data; it records the reasons people give, not whether those reasons are right.
